steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/markdown.py", "content": "class MarkdownContext:
    """Manages the console render state."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        console: Console,
        options: ConsoleOptions,
        style: Style,
        inline_code_lexer: Optional[str] = None,
        inline_code_theme: str = "monokai",
    ) -> None:
        self.console = console
        self.options = options
        self.style_stack: StyleStack = StyleStack(style)
        self.stack: Stack[MarkdownElement] = Stack()

        self._syntax: Optional[Syntax] = None
        if inline_code_lexer is not None:
            self._syntax = Syntax("", inline_code_lexer, theme=inline_code_theme)

    @property
    def current_style(self) -> Style:
        """Current style which is the product of all styles on the stack."""
        return self.style_stack.current

    def on_text(self, text: str, node_type: str) -> None:
        """Called when the parser visits text."""
        if node_type in {"fence", "code_inline"} and self._syntax is not None:
            highlight_text = self._syntax.highlight(text)
            highlight_text.rstrip()
            self.stack.top.on_text(
                self, Text.assemble(highlight_text, style=self.style_stack.current)
            )
        else:
            self.stack.top.on_text(self, text)

    def enter_style(self, style_name: Union[str, Style]) -> Style:
        """Enter a style context."""
        style = self.console.get_style(style_name, default="none")
        self.style_stack.push(style)
        return self.current_style

    def leave_style(self) -> Style:
        """Leave a style context."""
        style = self.style_stack.pop()
        return style


class Markdown(JupyterMixin):
    """A Markdown renderable.

    Args:
        markup (str): A string containing markdown.
        code_theme (str, optional): Pygments theme for code blocks. Defaults to "monokai".
        justify (JustifyMethod, optional): Justify value for paragraphs. Defaults to None.
        style (Union[str, Style], optional): Optional style to apply to markdown.
        hyperlinks (bool, optional): Enable hyperlinks. Defaults to ``True``.
        inline_code_lexer: (str, optional): Lexer to use if inline code highlighting is
            enabled. Defaults to None.
        inline_code_theme: (Optional[str], optional): Pygments theme for inline code
            highlighting, or None for no highlighting. Defaults to None.
    """

    elements: ClassVar[Dict[str, Type[MarkdownElement]]] = {
        "paragraph_open": Paragraph,
        "heading_open": Heading,
        "fence": CodeBlock,
        "code_block": CodeBlock,
        "blockquote_open": BlockQuote,
        "hr": HorizontalRule,
        "bullet_list_open": ListElement,
        "ordered_list_open": ListElement,
        "list_item_open": ListItem,
        "image": ImageItem,
        "table_open": TableElement,
        "tbody_open": TableBodyElement,
        "thead_open": TableHeaderElement,
        "tr_open": TableRowElement,
        "td_open": TableDataElement,
        "th_open": TableDataElement,
    }

    inlines = {"em", "strong", "code", "s"}

    def __init__(
        self,
        markup: str,
        code_theme: str = "monokai",
        justify: Optional[JustifyMethod] = None,

        hyperlinks: bool = True,

    ) -> None:
        parser = MarkdownIt().enable("strikethrough").enable("table")
        self.markup = markup
        self.parsed = parser.parse(markup)
        self.code_theme = code_theme
        self.justify: Optional[JustifyMethod] = justify
        self.style = style
        self.hyperlinks = hyperlinks
        self.inline_code_lexer = inline_code_lexer
        self.inline_code_theme = inline_code_theme or code_theme

    def _flatten_tokens(self, tokens: Iterable[Token]) -> Iterable[Token]:
        """Flattens the token stream."""
        for token in tokens:
            is_fence = token.type == "fence"
            is_image = token.tag == "img"
            if token.children and not (is_image or is_fence):
                yield from self._flatten_tokens(token.children)
            else:
                yield token

        self, console: Console, options: ConsoleOptions

import io
import re

from rich.console import Console, RenderableType
from rich.markdown import Markdown

re_link_ids = re.compile(r"id=[\d\.\-]*?;.*?\x1b")


def replace_link_ids(render: str) -> str:
    """Link IDs have a random ID and system path which is a problem for
    reproducible tests.

    """
    return re_link_ids.sub("id=0;foo\x1b", render)


def render(renderable: RenderableType) -> str:
    console = Console(
        width=100, file=io.StringIO(), color_system="truecolor", legacy_windows=False
    )
    console.print(renderable)
    output = replace_link_ids(console.file.getvalue())
    print(repr(output))
    return output
